                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution promotes and recognises staff mobility</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By taking it into account in the assessment of their professional development </span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Participation in international projects should be seen as an important aspect of the professional development of the staff and of the modernisation of the HEI and should, therefore, be considered a key component in staff evaluation practices.</p><p>The HEI should link its HR strategy to the objectives set out the internationalisation strategy for staff. For all staff who undertake a period of mobility, HR should be informed and provide support to ensure the identification of the professional development needs of the individual as well as setting out agreed career objectives for their period of mobility. This can be through prepared addendums to staff contracts or through less formal mechanisms of agreed objectives. The new objectives should become part of the normal system of staff evaluation or appraisal and be used in order to recognise the achievements of the staff during the period of mobility. This means that HR staff should be trained to ensure these additional objectives are formally evidenced and recorded in staff records and lead to other rewards and recognition.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Through, for example the reduction of the teaching load, promotion or pay rises</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important to incentivise staff to participate in mobility activities. In order to support and encourage mobility, HEIs should provide a number of incentives to ensure that when staff return to the sending institution, they have long term career benefits. HEIs should acknowledge periods of mobility as a normal part of a career path. Staff working schedules and agreed objectives (in terms of research outputs and assessments) should be adapted to meet their new requirements. Temporary replacements should be found during the mobility period, where possible, to ensure continuity during the mobility period. Upon returning to the sending institution, incentives to maintain links with other institutions or networks should be put in place through providing the time to nurture new relationships (reduction in teaching or research loads, continued related objectives set in performance appraisals). The new objectives set with HR for the period of mobility should be ones which are explicitly recognised and rewarded through promotion, awards or pay rises. Additional cultural / language skills should be recognised as a component in any evaluation / assessment of the staff. This may be achieved by making it well-known that participation is a formal part of staff evaluation procedures, and may lead to improvements in both working conditions and promotion or broader career prospects.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose improvements to the institutional strategy for internationalisation and overarching structure, as well as for structural reform</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>One important form of recognition for staff, which is equally beneficial to the HEI is to encourage their involvement in improving internationalisation and structural reform within the institution. This includes the opportunity for staff to provide feedback into the management structures of departments and the overall institution. There should be a firm commitment - perhaps in writing - from the HEI to recognise and make use of constructive feedback as well as the appropriate forums for staff to engage with senior management to discuss their experiences and propose new ideas for improvement.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By inviting them to share new learning and teaching practices developed abroad with their peers in the institution</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The experience of staff should be valued and shared as an inspiration to others, by, for example, organising meetings and publishing articles where the mobile participants share their experience and the impact of mobility on their personal and professional development. Where staff are involved in teaching at host institutions, new learning and teaching practices can be brought back and shared with other staff members through seminars or presentations. Staff can be supported through the administrative and academic services to understand the skills they have acquired and how best to use them within their own institution.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose cooperation projects with their receiving organisation</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Mobile staff bring back new partners, networks and ideas which can be of significant value for the HEI. Staff should be encouraged to propose and develop new or further cooperation projects between their receiving and sending institutions. This requires time and commitment, which need to be given formally by the sending institution, including, for example, additional support to write joint proposals.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-mobility-supporting-individuals-development-and-institutional-aims-and-objectives" target="_blank">Recognition of staff mobility – supporting individuals’ development and institutional aims and objectives</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-participating-in-erasmus-staff-mobility-actions-and-international-cooperation-projects" target="_blank">Recognition of staff participating in Erasmus staff mobility actions and international cooperation projects</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>
            </div>
                         <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">14</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> With regards to the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are monitored, evaluated and disseminated as a way to improve international cooperation and mobility activities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Linked with the overall internationalisation strategy of the institution, monitoring and evaluation of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility is essential if HEIs are to learn from their experiences. Monitoring and evaluation is more than just measuring the number and types of outputs, it needs to include capturing information on the overall outcomes and experiences of the activities at the institutional and the individual level. Systematic monitoring and evaluation should therefore include more qualitative approaches, which expressly capture the experiences in a way which helps the institution to understand the added value of its involvement in these activities. Documenting and analysing the outcomes and experiences is only the first step. To learn from the approaches taken, and the benefits gained, institutions should take time to disseminate the findings of the cooperation projects and mobility periods through, for example, meetings, workshops and publications, social media, etc. These activities will embed good practice, help the institution to iteratively improve its approach and also feed back into the on-going monitoring and evaluation.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are used systematically for the benefit of your institution, providing internationalisation at home, hence enhancing intercultural competences of non-mobile students and staff</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The outcomes and experiences of cooperation and Erasmus+ mobility have a much wider impact than just improving mobile activities. All institutions have significant numbers of non-mobile staff and students who can benefit from the international experiences of others. As part of the monitoring and evaluation processes, HEIs should consider the impact which can be specifically made on non-mobile staff and students, giving them “internationalisation at home experiences”. This includes building international competences, cultural awareness, virtual mobility opportunities, inviting international lecturers and embedding student projects with an international focus into the curricula, and providing opportunities for local students to work together with incoming mobile participants in e.g. project work, to ensure that local students benefit from the presence of mobile students at their institution. This fits with the activities of disseminating the overall outcomes and experiences of the cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility, though tailored to a different audience. It should take into account the professional development needs of the staff at the HEI and the perspectives of non-mobile students.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are exploited and disseminated, by providing participants with the results of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility opportunities (e.g. presentations) to share funding possibilities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">After the mobility Erasmus+ participants have the opportunity to present their newly acquired competences</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The study entitled ‘Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions’ showcases how mobility can contribute to the internationalisation of higher education institutions, including the impacts on teaching methods, cooperation between HEIs and perception of staff more generally. Therefore the dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/capitalising-on-the-outcomes-and-experiences-of-erasmus-activities" target="_blank">Capitalising on the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</a></div>

                                             </div>

<span><span>holbobe</span></span>

    About Pleo

    Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

    The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

    Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

    About the role

    The Creative Production studio team sits squarely within our Brand function working alongside our Brand Foundations team. You will report directly to the Director of Brand Strategy & Experience and join a tight-knit, highly experienced group of project management leads and producers.

    In this role, you will lead our internal Creative Production studio team, the execution engine delivering all branded assets across Pleo, including campaign and performance assets, global adaptation and localization, event branding, content marketing, web, socials and lifecycle design. You will balance hands-on delivery with direct people management for a team of three in-house designers and copywriter, ensuring our creative output remains fast, scalable, and sharp across all touchpoints.

    Who you’ll be working with and reporting to

    Our Brand department is 13 people across two teams: Brand Foundations and Creative Production. You'll lead the four-person Creative Production studio, a senior copywriter, two senior designers and a motion designer, spread across our European offices. Day to day, you'll work alongside a peer project lead on Brand Foundations, a brand strategist, our producers, and internal partners in Events, Lifecycle, Performance Marketing, HR/People Ops and Legal, plus our media agency. Most of the studio's clients are internal teams across Pleo.

    What you’ll be doing

    As a Senior Creative Project Manager, you will:

    Creative Production & Operations

    • Studio Ownership: Lead end-to-end execution across all creative production studio work streams, ensuring projects hit quality benchmarks, deadlines, and brand standards. This is also not just intake of brand requests but also spotting opportunities proactively for brand involvement and governance across the business.

    • Project Management: Own intake of BAU requests, filtering and assigning work while acting as the bridge between requestors and the studio team. Define scope upfront and ensure the team has what it needs to execute. Contribute to project plans for integrated campaigns and large events and manage Creative studio kick-offs, status reporting, and timeline and milestone tracking.

    • Core Output Focus: Oversee production for high-performing marketing assets, market localization and adaptations, event branding, and content marketing.

    • Process & Integration: Partner closely with peer project leads, producers, and the Brand Foundations team to streamline intake briefs, cross-team handoffs, and resource sharing.

    • Global Asset Delivery: Manage asset adaptation frameworks to keep our brand consistent across different regions and channels.

    • Capacity Planning: Own and manage resourcing across internal teams and freelance support, balancing capacity against demand and prioritizing against business needs when demands compete.

    • External agency partnerships: Serve as the lead creative point of contact for asset production with our media agency. Manage sprint-style monthly asset delivery in response to agency and internal performance team briefs, keeping output aligned with the media plan. Review final creative placements across Meta and LinkedIn to ensure assets display correctly on paid channels.

    People Management & Leadership

    • Direct Management: Line manage, mentor, and foster career growth for a cross-functional team of three in-house designers and one copywriter overseeing their daily priorities and bandwidth.

    Stakeholder Alignment & Strategy

    • Cross-Functional Partner: Serve as the strategic operational bridge connecting the studio with Marketing, Events, HR/People Ops, and Legal.

    • Leadership Alignment: Work closely with the Director of Brand Strategy & Experience and Associate Director of Brand Management to align studio output with broader brand goals and business priorities.

    We launched our new brand in September, so this is a moment to build. The studio has the basics in place, but intake, briefing, project tracking and resourcing are still early. You'll set the ways of working that the studio runs on, and we'd love you to bring AI into how we plan, brief and produce.

    What you bring


    You'll thrive in this role if you have:

    • In-House Brand Experience: Minimum 5-7 years of work experience. Solid background working in-house in a fast-paced brand function (tech, scale-up, or high-growth environment).

    • People Leadership: Direct experience line-managing creative talent (designers/artworkers) based remotely in different offices in Europe with an empathetic, growth-oriented approach.

    • Production Scope: Broad familiarity managing workflows across digital performance, multi-market localization, physical/virtual events, AI creative production, and employer branding.

    • Culture Driver: Thrives in a peer environment working alongside other motivated and constructive senior PMs, producers, creatives, and strategists.

    • Operational Skills: Mastery of modern project management tooling and AI-powered workflows (e.g. Asana, Notion, Jira, Slack).

    • Project Management Experience: Strong hands-on project management experience in a fast-paced, delivery-focused environment, running multiple projects concurrently. Comfortable not just initiating projects, but staying a consistent presence throughout: managing delivery, and reassessing priorities and capacity as needs shift.

    Why is this role a good fit for you

    This role is a good fit for you if:

    • You love day-to-day production and get a kick out of turning an event brief into finished collateral within a week.

    • You want to build how a studio works, from intake to resourcing, as much as you want to ship the work.

    • You enjoy leading creatives, giving them clear briefs and keeping the work grounded in what the business needs.

    This role is not a good fit for you if:

    • You mainly want to work on big brand campaigns. We run around two a year, and they're produced with an external agency. The studio adapts those assets, but most of the work is events, performance creative and BAU requests.

    • You prefer a predictable, planned workload. Last-minute requests are part of life on Brand.

    • You haven't line-managed people yet. Direct people management of the studio team is a core part of this role.

    How you’ll develop in this role

    In your first 6 months at Pleo, you'll:

    • Deliver the studio's day-to-day work to our speed and quality standards, in line with the new brand guidelines.

    • Set best practice for how the studio takes in, briefs, tracks and resources work.

    • Improve how we estimate and plan capacity, using AI where it makes sense.

    The location

    Please note: We can hire on a remote, hybrid or in-person set-up in any of the locations listed on the advert but you will need to be physically based in the country of your choice with a valid right to work. We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role in any of the listed locations.

    Show me the benefits!

    • Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)

    • Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office

    • Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis

    • We offer 25 days of holiday + your public holidays

    • For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options

    • Option to purchase 5 additional days of holiday through a salary sacrifice

    • We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far

    • Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work


    The interview process

    We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:

    • Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.

    • Hiring manager interview: A conversation with the Director about the projects you've delivered, the teams you've led and the kind of production work you enjoy most.

    • Case study: You'll walk us through how you'd approach a creative production task. You'll present to the Director and a peer project lead, and possibly a member of the studio team.

    • Final stage: Team-fit chat with one or two people from the studio

    Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!

    Last time we hired this role, we received an incredibly high volume of applications but only so many could be taken forward. Some of the key reasons why previous candidates didn’t make it past the application screening stage include:

    • CV writing and content: we receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background!

    • Application care: every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process.

    • Profile to role fit: highlight most important aspects of the role, points that might get misunderstood, any specific industry requirements etc.

    About your application

    • English first. Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us.

    • A fair look for everyone. Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails.

    • Diversity drives us. We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us.

    • Interview at your best. We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email ----- We’ll design a process that works for you.

    • Your data is safe. When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here.

    • Applying for multiple roles? Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role.

    • Reapplying. If you’re applying for the same role again, please wait six months from your last decision before hitting submit.

    Data Enablement Officer

    What you'll be doing

    Establish our data governance framework

    • Client data handling and classification

    • Retention, archiving and secure disposal

    • Third-party data sharing

    • Policy exceptions and escalation

    You will also help establish and maintain our information asset inventories, data flows and AI asset registers.

    Enable responsible use of data and AI

    A key part of the role will be helping teams determine what we can do with data, under what conditions, and with what safeguards.

    You will establish a consistent approach for assessing new and changing data use cases, considering factors such as:

    • The proposed use and intended recipients

    • Security and access controls

    • Retention requirements

    • Legal, client and reputational considerations

    • Encryption, access controls and logging

    • Supplier and subcontractor access

    • Data retention, backups and deletion

    • Use of customer data for AI model training, product improvement or other secondary purposes

    This role isn't simply about writing policies. We want to create a governance model that teams can understand and use.

    À propos de notre client

    Notre client est une TPE basée au nord de Lyon, spécialisée dans les énergies du sous-sol : pétrole, gaz, géothermie et stockage de CO2. Son activité repose entièrement sur la R&D : essais sur géomatériaux, géomécanique et développement d'équipements d'essais pour des clients internationaux.

    Le poste

    Pour accélérer ses projets de développement, notre client recrute un(e) Ingénieur(e) R&D en conception d'équipements d'essais.  Vous prendrez en charge la conception, la mise au point et la validation de cellules d'essais haute température et haute pression, un sujet stratégique pour l'entreprise et ses clients.

    Rattaché(e) à la direction des opérations, vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec l'équipe qui conçoit aujourd'hui les équipements et dépose les brevets de l'entreprise.

    Répartition indicative du temps : environ 70 à 80 % conception et développement, 20 à 30 % laboratoire (montage et validation de vos équipements).

    Dans une structure à taille humaine, vous suivrez vos développements de la conception jusqu'aux tests, avant leur transfert à l'équipe de production.

    Vos missions

    Conception et développement d'équipements d’essais

    • Concevoir de nouvelles cellules et de nouveaux dispositifs d'essais, notamment pour des conditions de haute température et de haute pression.
    • Résoudre les problématiques techniques associées : instrumentation et capteurs, étanchéité, tenue en température et en pression.
    • Consulter les fournisseurs et sous-traitants, et suivre la fabrication des pièces.
    • Améliorer les équipements existants, notamment leur ergonomie et leur facilité d'utilisation en production.

    Mise au point et validation

    • Monter les équipements développés et réaliser leurs tests de validation au laboratoire.
    • Interpréter les résultats expérimentaux et vérifier leur cohérence.
    • Transférer les équipements validés à l'équipe de production et l'accompagner dans leur prise en main.

    Documentation et propriété intellectuelle

    • Rédiger la documentation technique, les rapports et les comptes-rendus, et les présenter, en français comme en anglais.
    • Participer à la veille technique et à la rédaction des documents de protection (brevets, enveloppes Soleau).

    Vie du laboratoire

    • Comprendre les essais réalisés au laboratoire pour concevoir des équipements adaptés à leurs besoins.
    • Contribuer à l'activité du labo et à l'amélioration continue, dans le respect de la démarche qualité ISO 9001.

    Requirements

    Compétences techniques

    • Conception mécanique et maîtrise d'un logiciel de CAO.
    • Instrumentation, capteurs et techniques de mesure.
    • Compréhension des grandeurs physiques et physico-chimiques.
    • Rédaction technique et anglais professionnel, à l'oral comme à l'écrit.

    Savoir-être

    • Autonomie et capacité à prendre en main un sujet de bout en bout.
    • Rigueur, notamment dans les phases d'essais.
    • Polyvalence et goût du concret : vous aimez concevoir autant que tester vous-même vos équipements.
    • Communication proactive, en particulier pour remonter et résoudre les difficultés rencontrées.
    • Envie d'apprendre et de s'investir dans une petite structure.

    Formation et expérience

    • Diplôme d'ingénieur ou équivalent Bac +5 en génie mécanique, conception, instrumentation ou mesures physiques.
    • Expérience d'environ 5 ans en conception d'équipements, en bureau d'études ou en R&D. Les profils plus juniors avec une première expérience significative en conception seront étudiés.
    • Une expérience sur des équipements soumis à des contraintes de température ou de pression est un vrai plus.

    Benefits

    Vous rejoindrez une entreprise à taille humaine où chaque développement compte : vos équipements seront directement utilisés pour des projets de R&D menés pour des clients internationaux. Vous travaillerez au sein d'une équipe dynamique et multiculturelle, sur des sujets techniques exigeants au service des énergies du sous-sol et de la transition énergétique.

    About EH Group Engineering

    EHG is developing cutting-edge fuel cell technology for heavy duty mobility and large-scale stationary power applications. Our uniquely redesigned product is a significantly more compact fuel cell with high power density and lower costs of production. Faced with the challenges of climate change and the transition to a decentralised energy system, EHG seeks to provide high performance and cost-effective fuel cell solutions to our clients and partners.

    To help bring this vision to life, we are looking for a Senior Control Engineer to coordinate our efforts in designing control strategies for containerized systems integrating our fuel cell technology alongside equipment such as gas reformers, batteries, and climate control units. You will coordinate the control team and play a key role in shaping how these complex, multi-equipment systems operate safely and efficiently in the field.

    Based in the US? You’re welcome to apply. This is an on-site role in Nyon, Switzerland. We ask that you relocate within 3 months of starting, and we’ll support you with a relocation package.

     

    Key Responsibilities:

    • Coordinate the control engineering activities and define the control architecture and technical roadmap for our fuel cell and containerized power systems

    • Develop control strategies, models and algorithms for test-benches, fuel cell system and containerized power supply systems using Matlab/Simulink and Siemens PLCs

    • Coordinate the transition of prototype control algorithms from Simulink to industrial-quality code in TIA Portal Step 7

    • Implement, tune and validate controllers for thermal, air, fuel and power subsystems

    • Define and own control requirements, state machines and safety/diagnostic logic

    • Drive the continuous improvement (performance, efficiency and robustness) of our products

    • Define and oversee model-in-the-loop (MIL) testing and validation procedures

    • Manage the complete software life cycle, from requirements through release and maintenance, including dataset management

    • Establish coding standards, conduct code reviews and ensure compliance with industrial and certification requirements

    • Coordinate and develop the control team, including task planning and prioritization

    • Act as the main control interface with embedded, test and electrical engineering, as well as external partners and suppliers

     

    Skills and Experience Required:

    • BSc/MSc in control, electrical, mechatronic or automation engineering is mandatory

    • Minimum 7 years of experience in control engineering, including at least 2 years in a technical lead or senior role

    • Skill 1 : Strong experience in process control engineering, particularly with containerized power supply systems; knowledge of programming and implementing safety PLCs is a strong plus

    • Skill 2 : Strong experience with TIA Portal (Step 7, WinCC, Test Suite), with the ability to structure code to industrial standards and meet certification requirements

    • Experience with functional safety (e.g. IEC 61508, ISO 13849), including SIL/PL determination and implementation of safety functions

    • Experience across the complete V-model development cycle, including hazard and risk assessment, requirements definition, safety requirements specification (SRS), verification and validation, and dataset management

    • Experience with stationary and maritime power applications, with a focus on the US and EU markets and their respective standards and certification requirements

    • Proven team player, with the ability to:
      (i) Coordinate and mentor the control team by clearly explaining your code and helping the team adopt robust industrial methods: you will take the responsibility in developing Skill 1 and Skill 2 across the team
      (ii) Collaborate effectively within interdisciplinary teams

    • Solid knowledge of control theory, state machines and system identification

    • Strong experience with MATLAB/Simulink and model-based design is a plus

    • Professional working language is in English.

       

    Start date: Immediately

    About EHG

    EH Group (EHG) is a rapidly growing fuel cell power platform delivering onsite power to AI data centers, defense, and industry. Our fuel-agnostic proton exchange membrane (PEM) systems scale from kW-scale units to GW-scale power plants, and we design, manufacture, and deploy them for customers worldwide.

    Founded in Switzerland, EHG is now expanding into the United States, fueled by exponential AI data center power demand and a soon-to-be-announced major investment round. This is a defining, high-growth chapter for the company.

     

    The opportunity

    We're hiring a Quality Manager to own a single quality system across both of our production streams — our established MW-scale facility in Nyon, Switzerland and our new US operation in Houston, Texas.

    You'd be based in Nyon, where our production and process knowledge sits today, and own quality for the US operation as it stands up. The requirement is explicit: quality must be identical at both sites. Same specifications, same control plans, same acceptance criteria, same records. A customer taking delivery of a system should not be able to tell which site built the stack inside it, and our certification and warranty position depends on being able to demonstrate that.

    Our customers are data center operators, defense programs, and industrial sites where reliability is the product. In your first year you'd harmonize our quality management system across both entities, establish controls in Houston that match those proven in Nyon as manufacturing technology transfers, build supplier quality alongside Supply Chain for a shared global supply base, and support certification of our systems for both European and US markets.

    Location & travel: Nyon-based. Regular travel to Houston is expected as the US operation stands up, along with travel to supplier and partner sites in Europe and the US.

     

    What you'll own

    • One quality management system across both entities — a common QMS covering Nyon and Houston, including the path to ISO 9001 certification in the US and alignment with what is already established in Switzerland.

    • Equivalence between sites. A single set of product specifications, control plans, inspection criteria, and acceptance standards, with a defined process for how any change is applied at both sites rather than one.

    • In-process quality for fuel cell stack production at both locations, including the process controls that matter most in stack assembly — cleanliness and contamination control, leak testing, torque and compression control, and alignment.

    • Supplier quality for a shared global supply base, working with Supply Chain on qualification, audits, first article inspection, part submission, and ongoing performance, with one qualification standard regardless of which site a supplier serves.

    • Quality oversight of contract manufacturing and assembly partners building balance of plant and containerized systems on our behalf in both regions — audits, quality agreements, source inspection, and acceptance criteria.

    • Nonconformance and corrective action across both sites, including NCR and CAPA processes and structured problem solving, with findings at one site systematically applied at the other.

    • Traceability and product records — a common lot genealogy model from raw material through stack serial to delivered system, and the test and inspection data that supports warranty, certification, and customer acceptance, held consistently across both entities.

    • Certification across regions, working with external certification partners on the standards applicable to stationary hydrogen power systems in Europe and the US, authority having jurisdiction approvals, and marine classification where relevant.

    • Quality culture on both floors, including operator training, work instruction discipline, and establishing the habits in Houston that are already proven in Nyon, as US headcount grows quickly.

    • Building the US quality capability, defining what needs to sit on the ground in Houston versus what is run centrally from Nyon, and recruiting into it as volumes grow.

     

    What we're looking for

    Core experience

    • Owning quality across more than one manufacturing site, ideally in more than one country, with a demonstrated ability to hold two sites to genuinely the same standard from a distance.

    • Establishing or substantially rebuilding a quality function, including authoring a quality management system rather than administering an existing one.

    • Hands-on in-process and incoming quality in a production setting, with real familiarity with control plans, inspection methods, measurement systems, and process capability.

    • Supplier quality experience, including auditing suppliers and holding them to standard.

    • Structured problem solving and root cause analysis, with a track record of permanently closing out recurring defects.

    • Working knowledge of product certification processes and the evidence they require, ideally in energy, power equipment, or another regulated product category. Exposure to both European and US regimes is a strong advantage.

    • The judgment to know which controls are essential at low volume and which can wait, and the confidence to hold a quality position under schedule pressure.

    • Comfort working across time zones and influencing a site you are not physically based at, including building quality capability remotely.

    Especially compelling

    • Fuel cell, battery cell, or similar electrochemical assembly experience.

    • Experience with cleanliness-critical or contamination-sensitive assembly processes.

    • Experience supporting a technology transfer between sites or countries, and establishing quality at the receiving end.

    • Experience qualifying and auditing contract manufacturers or system integrators.

    • Startup or scale-up experience as an early hire during hyper-growth.

    • Experience working between Europe and the US, and with US codes and certification practice in particular. French is useful but not required.

     

    What we offer

    • Competitive compensation and meaningful equity, calibrated to the market and discussed directly with you.

    • Relocation support to Nyon, Switzerland.

    • The opportunity to build EHG's global quality function during a defining phase of hyper-growth.

    Note: Swiss work authorization or eligibility is required for this role, along with the ability to travel to the United States.

    • Share expertise, lessons learned, and best practices to strengthen team capability, collaboration, product quality, reliability, and continuous improvement.

Jobbeschreibung

Du hast die Paid-Social-Landschaft fest im Griff und nutzt KI im Kampagnenmanagement nicht als Hype, sondern als tägliches Werkzeug? Du möchtest datengetriebene Entscheidungen treffen, kreative Kampagnen entwickeln und aktiv mitgestalten, wie modernste AI-Tools Analyse, Reporting und Kreation im E-Commerce revolutionieren? Dann wartet in unserem Team in Berlin deine nächste große Challenge auf dich: Bei benuta übernimmst du echte Ownership für unsere Paid-Social-Kanäle und treibst ein echtes Greenfield-Thema voran – die Skalierung KI-gestützter Analysen, Workflows und Strategien für den europäischen Marktführer im Home-&-Living-Bereich!

Deine Aufgaben

  • Strategische Paid-Social-Steuerung: Du entwickelst und verantwortest die kanalübergreifende Paid-Social-Media-Strategie zur Erreichung unserer Unternehmensziele (Brand Awareness, Lead-Gen, Performance-Ziele) und richtest sie an der übergreifenden Marketingstrategie aus.
  • Kampagnenmanagement & Kanal-Synergien: Du bist verantwortlich für die Erstellung, das Monitoring und die Optimierung unserer Paid-Social-Kampagnen (Schwerpunkt Meta, Pinterest, Reddit Ads und TikTok) und arbeitest eng mit den Kolleg*innen aus Google Ads und Bing Ads für eine ganzheitliche Performance-Sicht zusammen.
  • AI-Integration & Workflow-Innovation: Du treibst den Einsatz von LLMs (z. B. Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT) für die automatisierte Analyse und Auswertung unserer Kampagnendaten aktiv voran. Du entwickelst Prompts und Workflows für beschleunigtes Reporting, Anomalie-Erkennung sowie Optimierungen und agierst als interner Expert für KI-gestützte Marketing-Tools.
  • Kreative Nutzung von KI: Du nutzt generative KI gezielt für Anzeigentexte, Variantentests und Creative-Ideation. In engem Austausch mit dem Design- und Content-Team gibst du als Senior-Ansprechperson fachlichen Input und Feedback.
  • Analyse & Tracking-Setup: Du überwachst und analysierst die Kampagnen-Performance anhand von KPIs (CTR, KUR, ROAS, Conversion Rate) unter Nutzung unseres MMM. Du implementierst Tracking-Tools (Pixel, UTM-Parameter, Conversion-APIs) und stellst eine saubere Datengrundlage sicher.
  • Testing: Du verantwortest das fortlaufende A/B-Testing von Anzeigenformaten, Zielgruppen sowie Budgets und bewertest neue Werbemöglichkeiten sowie KI-Werbeprodukte auf ihr Potenzial für benuta.
  • Mentoring: Du unterstützt bei der fachlichen Anleitung sowie dem Onboarding von Junior-Kolleg*innen im Team und teilst dein KI-Wissen.

Stellenanforderungen

Dein Profil

  • Ausbildung: Du hast dein Studium (BWL, Marketing, Medien, Kommunikationswissenschaften o. Ä.) erfolgreich abgeschlossen oder bringst eine vergleichbare Qualifikation mit.

  • AI-Expertise (Must-have): Du besitzt praxiserprobte Erfahrung im Einsatz von KI-Tools und LLMs im Marketing-Kontext (z. B. Prompting für Reporting, Kampagnenanalysen oder Creative-Unterstützung). Du verfolgst aktuelle AI-Trends aktiv und brennst darauf, eigene Ideen bei benuta einzubringen.
  • Hard Skills: Du besitzt sehr gute Kenntnisse im Meta-Werbeanzeigenmanager und zeichnest dich durch ausgeprägte analytische Fähigkeiten im Umgang mit gängigen Reporting-/Attributions-Tools aus. Erfahrung mit Pinterest, Reddit, TikTok, Bing Ads und serverseitigem Tracking ist ein Plus.
  • Soft Skills: Du arbeitest datengetrieben, denkst lösungsorientiert und begeisterst dich für E-Commerce sowie die Themen Home & Living.
  • Sprachkompetenz: Deine Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse sind sehr gut (weitere Sprachen sind ein Plus).

Deine Benefits

  • Impact & Gestaltungsspielraum: Bei uns kannst du aktiv mitgestalten, die Marke benuta weiterentwickeln und spannende KI-Projekte umsetzen – wie etwa den Aufbau KI-gestützter Analyse-Workflows für unsere Kampagnendaten. Deine Ideen werden gehört und du bekommst Freiraum für die Umsetzung eigener Ansätze.
  • Präsenz & Flexibilität: Der Schwerpunkt unserer Arbeit liegt auf dem persönlichen Austausch und der gemeinsamen Zusammenarbeit vor Ort an unserem Standort in Berlin. Für die nötige Flexibilität in deiner Alltagsplanung - sei es für private Termine oder ungestörtes Arbeiten - bieten wir dir ein jährliches Kontingent von 26 Home-Office-Tagen.
  • Deine Mobilität: Egal wie du zu uns kommst, wir unterstützen dich. Du hast die Wahl zwischen einem vergünstigten Jobticket oder einer Tankkarte. Zudem bieten wir dir ein Firmenrad-Leasing (JobRad) und eine gute ÖPNV-Anbindung.
  • Zeit für Erholung: Du erhältst 28 Tage Urlaub und profitierst von unserem flexiblen Gleitzeitmodell. Weihnachten und Silvester sind bei uns grundsätzlich arbeitsfreie Tage, die nicht von deinem Urlaubskonto abgehen.
  • Deine Entwicklung: Unsere unterschiedlichen Abteilungen mit internationalen Teams arbeiten an vielfältigen Projekten zusammen. Dadurch lernst Du permanent neue Sichtweisen, Tools und Prozesse kennen – inklusive aktuellster KI-Anwendungen im Performance Marketing.
  • Kultur & Mitarbeitervorteile: Ein strukturiertes Onboarding, flache Hierarchien und attraktive Mitarbeiterrabatte warten auf dich. Bei uns gilt: Come as you are – fühl dich wohl und sei einfach du selbst!

Klingt nach deinem nächsten Match? Dann freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung! Lade einfach deinen Lebenslauf und deine relevanten Zeugnisse über unser Online-Portal hoch.

Dein Ansprechpartner ist Michael Stanke (Head of Online Marketing).

*Bei uns zählt der Mensch und seine Motivation - unabhängig von Geschlecht, Herkunft, Religion oder sexueller Orientierung. Bewerbungen von Menschen mit einer Schwerbehinderung oder ihnen Gleichgestellten werden bei gleicher Eignung bevorzugt berücksichtigt.

Über benuta

Seit 2008 revolutionieren wir von Bonn aus den europäischen Teppich- und Home-&-Living-E-Commerce. Mit über 100 Millionen Euro Umsatz, modernster AI-gestützter Produktinszenierung und Kunden in 17 Ländern verbinden wir die Sicherheit eines etablierten Marktführers mit dem Drive und den flachen Hierarchien eines Digital-Pioneers. Unser Ziel ist einfach: Jedes Zuhause noch schöner zu machen. Werde Teil unseres Teams und hilf uns dabei, noch mehr Menschen für unsere Produkte zu begeistern.

    We are looking for an experienced contractor to lead the analysis, design and execution of a data migration from one Salesforce instance (source org) to another (target org), using Microsoft SQL Server as the staging and transformation layer. You will own the end-to-end migration data workstream: profiling source data, mapping objects and fields, building transformation logic, loading and reconciling data, and supporting cutover.

    This is a hands-on, delivery-focused role. The right person will combine strong Salesforce data model knowledge with proven, real-world experience of moving data between orgs safely and accurately. The role can be filled at Data Analyst or Data Architect level depending on the candidate’s experience; architect-level candidates will additionally be expected to shape the overall migration approach and standards.


    Main Duties / Responsibilities:
  • Define and document the data migration approach, scope, and sequencing for moving data between Salesforce orgs, including cutover and rollback considerations.
  • Analyse and profile source Salesforce data to assess volumes, quality, duplication, and dependencies across standard and custom objects.
  • Produce object-level and field-level mapping documents between source and target orgs, covering data types, picklist values, record types, required fields, and validation rules.
  • Design and maintain SQL Server staging databases and schemas to extract, cleanse, transform, and stage Salesforce data ahead of loading.
  • Write, optimise, and test T-SQL (stored procedures, views, ETL logic) to implement transformation and data-cleansing rules.
  • Manage the migration of parent/child relationships and record ownership, preserving referential integrity through ID cross-referencing (source ID to target ID) and correct load order.
  • Extract and load data using appropriate tooling (e.g., Salesforce Data Loader, Bulk API, SSIS, Azure Data Factory, dbAmp, or equivalent) and manage error handling and re-runs.
  • Plan and run multiple migration cycles (development, test/UAT, and production dress rehearsals) and execute the production cutover.
  • Design and run reconciliation and validation checks (record counts, field-level comparisons, sampling) and produce sign-off evidence for business stakeholders.
  • Work with Salesforce administrators, developers, business analysts, and data owners to resolve data quality issues and agree transformation rules.
  • Identify and manage migration risks and issues, including data volume limits, API limits, automation and trigger impacts, and sharing/ownership considerations.
  • Ensure the handling of personal data complies with GDPR and internal data governance and security standards.
  • Produce clear documentation and a handover pack (mapping specifications, scripts, runbooks, lessons learned) so the migration can be supported after your engagement ends.

    • Essential Skills & Qualifications:
  • Proven, hands-on experience delivering data migrations between Salesforce orgs or from other systems into Salesforce, ideally including at least one full production cutover.
  • Strong working knowledge of the Salesforce data model, including standard objects (e.g., Account, Contact, Lead, Opportunity, Case, User) and custom objects, relationships (lookup and master-detail), record types, and field types.
  • Strong SQL Server and T-SQL skills, including stored procedures, joins across large data sets, performance tuning, and data quality checks.
  • Experience with data extraction and loading tools for Salesforce (e.g., Data Loader, Bulk API, SSIS, Azure Data Factory, Informatica, Talend, Boomi, dbAmp, or similar).
  • Solid experience in data profiling, cleansing, deduplication, and mapping, with a methodical approach to reconciliation and audit trails.
  • Understanding of Salesforce migration considerations such as ownership and sharing, validation rules, triggers/flows, API limits, and managing record IDs across orgs.
  • Awareness of data privacy requirements (e.g., GDPR) and secure handling of customer data.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate technical data concepts for business stakeholders and to work independently in a fast-paced delivery environment.

  • Salesforce certifications (e.g., Salesforce Certified Data Architecture and Management Designer, Administrator, or Platform App Builder).

    About Allica Bank

    Allica is the UK’s fastest growing company - and the fastest-growing financial technology (Fintech) firm ever. Our purpose is to help established SMEs, one of the last major underserved opportunities in Fintech.

    Established SMEs are the backbone of local communities - representing over a third of our economy - yet have been largely neglected both by traditional high street banks and modern fintech providers.

    Department Description

    Payments is where our customers feel Allica every single day. We’ve built an award-winning business current account for established SMEs that pairs genuinely great technology with bestin-class customer experience – and goes beyond payments to make running a business’s finances simple and painless.

    You’ll be part of the Payments Tribe, supporting the squads that together cover the full product. Product, engineering, design and data work side by side, in close partnership with Distribution, Operations, Compliance and Risk. Our job is to take the complex problems SMEs face, the ones the big banks have neglected for years, and solve them with simple, elegant products. If you want to see your work ship quickly and make a real difference to UK SMEs, this is the place to do it.

    Role Description

    • As Product Analyst, you’ll help shape and deliver our Business Rewards Account and its card and payment features, working alongside the Senior Product Owner and the wider Tribe.

    • You’ll turn data, customer feedback and business requirements into clear insight and well-defined user stories, so the squads build the right things – and builds them well.

    • Success looks like decisions backed by evidence, a sharp and well-prioritised backlog, and processes that are simpler and more automated than when you found them. 

    • It’s a great opportunity to learn product ownership inside a high-growth bank, with real scope to grow your product career.

    Principal Accountabilities

    • Support the Senior Product Owner in defining and delivering features for our business current account, from discovery through to release 

    • Gather, analyse and document requirements from Distribution, Operations, Compliance and Risk, turning them into clear user stories and acceptance criteria 

    • Help maintain and prioritise the squad and wider Tribe backlogs, keeping them aligned to the roadmap and product and business OKRs 

    • Track and report on product performance – such as balances, usage and customer behaviour – and surface insights that inform decisions 

    • Gather and analyse customer feedback, then propose and lead product improvements

    • Work day-to-day with engineers and designers to clarify requirements, answer questions and test what’s delivered 

    • Manage relationships with key vendors to keep delivery focused and on track

    • Map and improve processes, spotting opportunities to simplify and automate

    • Keep product documentation, tracking and risk logs accurate and up to date, flagging issues early 

    • Use AI tools to build and ship small changes to production

    Personal Attributes & Experience

    • Experience as a Business Analyst, Product Analyst or in a similar role (around 2+ years), ideally working on digital products in payments or financial services

    • Working knowledge of UK payment schemes (e.g. Faster Payments, Bacs, CHAPS) and card payments; awareness of payments regulation is a plus

    • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, and comfortable working with data – SQL or similar is a plus 

    • Great attention to detail, without losing sight of the bigger picture

    • Clear, concise written and verbal communication – able to explain complex things simply 

    • Organised and proactive, able to juggle priorities in a fast-moving or high-growth environment 

    • Exposure to Agile ways of working and tools such as Jira and Confluence 

    • Curious and keen to learn, with examples of where you’ve gone the extra mile, taken on a new challenge or stood out from your peers

    • A genuine curiosity about AI, with hands-on experience of experimenting with AI tools, at work or elsewhere 

    • A design-minded approach, with an eye for user experience

    At Allica Bank we want to ensure our employees have the right tools and environment in which to succeed in their role and in support of our customers.

    • Full onboarding support and continued development opportunities

    • Options for flexible working

    • Regular social activities

    • Pension contributions

    • Discretionary bonus scheme

    • Private health cover

    • Life assurance

    • Family friendly policies including enhanced Maternity & Paternity leave

    Don’t worry if you don’t have all the skills or requirements listed on the job description. If you think you’ll be a good fit, we’d still love to hear from you!

    We’re a diverse bunch here at Allica, with all kinds of experiences, backgrounds and lifestyles. Our openness and differences make us stronger, and we want everybody to feel comfortable bringing as much of themselves to work with them as they like.

    Customer Success Manager

    🌍 About us

    Plinth is a fast-growing tech startup working with charities, foundations and local government. Small and local charities are highly effective but largely hidden.     🤝You'll work with impressive people. Our team is talented, collaborative and slightly strange(?). We value impact, speed and openness.     💼 You need to be able to:

    • Work both fast and slow: You'll navigate slow public sector procurement cycles one minute, then help us ship a new feature over lunch the next. The whiplash is intense but it keeps things interesting.

    • Keep it real: You'll be getting the train to community centres and youth clubs where the heating doesn't work and where the paint is peeling off the walls. It’s rarely glamourous. You need to be willing to meet clients where they are, literally and figuratively.

    • Listen to problems, ignore solutions: Clients will tell you exactly what they think they need.     • Teach people: Most of our clients don't love shiny gadgets. If you're the kind of person who enjoys teaching your gran to use a smartphone, this is ideal. You need to explain some fairly complex systems clearly without being condescending and still getting user adoption

    • Automate and document yourself away:🤖 We're small and growing fast. Build systems and processes that make your job increasingly redundant. There’s always plenty more to do.

    • Understand the difference between "urgent" and 🚨 URGENT — When you're managing 4-8 concurrent client projects and everyone thinks their issue is critical, you need to distinguish between what must happen for launch versus what can wait. This is harder than it sounds.

    • Grow with the role: we need someone who is comfortable with our clients and team doubling every 6 months. Your role will rapidly change to reflect that, but it leaves you with lots of room to grow in responsibility.

    🧩 What kind of background do we think would be a good fit?

    We’d expect a few years experience in something like the following:

    • Coaching / Tutoring: You know how to meet people where they are and guide them to better outcomes

    • Hospitality management: Service mindset, de-escalation skills, managing expectations when things don't go to plan, letting the customer think they’re right when they aren’t

    • Event/production management: Used to juggling moving pieces, keeping stakeholders calm, making last-minute pivots when things go wrong

    • Community organising/activism: Already comfortable in the spaces you'll be visiting, get the mission, used to working with limited resources

    • Consulting: You're used to parachuting into chaos, extracting actionable tasks, and keeping multiple clients calm simultaneously

    • User research/UX: Good at understanding what people actually need versus what they say they need, synthesising feedback into actionable insights

    • Knowledge of the charity sector is a significant advantage, whether that’s as an employee, consultant or as a long term volunteer.

    • It would also definitely be helpful if you have any technical experience to help with managing data migrations.

    Importantly, This is a list of suggestions.

    If you have experience in only some of this, or have only some of these skills, please do apply anyway.

    📈 How can you measure your success?

    • Speed of getting customers successfully using Plinth: From signed contract to actively using the platform and seeing value.

    • Positive recommendations: Clients recommending us positively to their networks — it’s a big source of our growth.

    • Increasing use of Plinth: Clients expanding how they use the platform over time, not just maintaining baseline usage

    Client Onboarding (70%) — Lead onboarding from kick-off to go-live. Break down complex projects into clear phases. Manage timelines, priorities, and expectations across 7+ new clients per month. Stay on top of new features we ship every few days. Push back when needed and teach anyone regardless of background.

    Operations & Process Improvement (30%) — Audit and optimise our support systems (expect to manage Intercom chat a couple of days a week). Refine onboarding workflows. Keep documentation current.     • Salary: £42,000 - £75,000 depending on experience

    4. Decision

    About Nabla

    Nabla delivers a unified clinical AI platform used by healthcare organizations across specialties and care settings. The platform includes:

    Ambient AI documentation that captures clinical conversations and generates structured notes.

    AI-powered dictation and clinical workflow tools embedded directly within EHR systems.

    Agentic AI capabilities that support multi-step clinical and administrative tasks.

    Enterprise-grade infrastructure built for secure deployment across health systems.

    About the Role

    We are scaling our healthcare AI platform, with more products, integrations and AI agents, and more protected health information (PHI) flowing through them. To keep pace, we're growing our security engineering team and looking for an exceptional Senior Security Engineer.

    Our cloud infrastructure handles highly sensitive healthcare data, so security is core to everything we do. Our engineers already ask the right questions every day: can we use a one-time token here? How long should it live? How do we scope this OAuth Client?

    You'll work directly with our Lead Security Engineer to bring real AppSec expertise into the product squads, and to strengthen security well beyond them.

    This is a hands-on, high-impact role. About half your time goes to AppSec, but it is deliberately a broad security engineering role, not a pure code-review or pentest job. You'll regularly cross into platform and cloud, CI/CD and detection, and you'll own problems from start to finish. Code scanning, SCA and AI-driven code review are already running, but there is no AppSec process to undo. The threat-modeling practice, the security review loop, the triage rhythm and the secure-by-default libraries don't exist yet. You'll build them and run them.

    If you're pragmatic, love working shoulder to shoulder with developers, and want your work to protect patients' most sensitive data, this role is for you.

    Responsibilities

    • Partner with the product squads as their go-to security engineer: design reviews, per-feature threat modeling, and fast, opinionated answers on authN/authZ, tokens and session design.

    • Secure our authentication and authorization surfaces (OAuth clients, one-time codes, multi-org tenancy, the Core API user API, embedded/postMessage SDKs) and hunt for BOLA, IDOR and broken access control before attackers do.

    • Run the code-security findings loop: triage and prioritize results from our SAST, SCA, secrets and IaC scanners and AI-driven code review, route them to the right owners with SLAs, and drive the dependency-vulnerability backlog down, fixing issues yourself when that's faster.

    • Secure our AI/LLM features and internal agents, covering prompt injection, tool and permission scoping for autonomous agents, PHI leakage, de-identification assurance and model/API egress.

    • Run the external testing program: scope and run pentests (web, mobile, backoffice), validate fixes, operate our vulnerability disclosure program, and stand up a bug bounty.

    • Experience working in leading AI research environments

    Technical Mastery:

    • Deep expertise in PyTorch or JAX, experience with Transformers, Diffusion Models, and Large Language Models (LLMs).

    Domain Knowledge:

    • Strong understanding of Vision-Language models and their application to Action/Control loops in robotics.

    Location:

    • This role is based in our Zurich office, offering a vibrant ecosystem for robotics and AI.

    • Java Development

    • Kubernetes & Cloud Native

    • Cloud & Platform Engineering

    • Front-end Development

    • actief technische professionals sourcet en benadert, onder andere via LinkedIn Recruiter en andere sourcingkanalen;

    • zelfstandig searches en sourcingstrategieën ontwikkelt voor moeilijk vindbare doelgroepen;

    • interview- en selectieprocessen bewaakt en waar nodig bijstuurt;

The team

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

Join our Product and Regulatory Legal team, embedded with Kraken's Product, Design and Engineering teams to ship novel products and experiences that accelerate the global adoption of crypto. We are a tight, experienced group of lawyers from a diverse range of tradfi, fintech and crypto backgrounds who move fast, stay curious and take pride in the commercial accountability of our advice, partnering directly with Product, senior leadership and Compliance to chart clear, defensible paths to launch and to keep our licensed entities running smoothly.

This is a senior product-facing legal role for the European Union. You will be the lawyer the business trusts on questions that cut across several regimes at once: for example, a single product such as a tokenised equity, a card, or an institutional custody and prime brokerage service can touch the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive ("MiFID II"), the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation ("MiCA"), the Payment Services Directive ("PSD2"), the Electronic Money Directive ("EMD2") and banking rules at the same time. You will bring clarity on which regime applies, what it requires, and how to launch within it.

 

The opportunity

Reporting to the Head of Product Legal, you will act as a senior legal adviser to European leadership on new products, licensing structure and regulatory strategy.

  • Own cross-functional product counselling for European Union launches from discovery to design, launch and iteration, giving Product, Engineering, Compliance and leadership decision-ready advice with clear options and risk trade-offs

  • Advise on the regulatory perimeter and classification of new offerings across MiFID II and the Markets in Financial Instruments Regulation ("MiFIR"), MiCA, the European Market Infrastructure Regulation ("EMIR"), payment services and electronic money rules, and banking regulation, including where an instrument or service falls between regimes (for example tokenised securities, crypto-asset derivatives, margin and financing, and stablecoin-linked products)

  • Advise on payments and electronic money offerings, including the Krak card and account propositions, safeguarding, open banking and account-access obligations, and the developing Payment Services Directive 3 and Payment Services Regulation framework

  • Advise on banking-related questions that arise in the European Union, including bank partnerships and sponsor-bank arrangements, deposit-taking and lending perimeter questions, the Capital Requirements Regulation and Directive, and the interaction of these rules with our custody, prime brokerage and financing products

  • Monitor and interpret European Union legislative and supervisory developments, take part in consultations and industry association work where appropriate, and translate their significance for the business proactively

  • Draft and negotiate client-facing terms and conditions, taking clear, business-aligned positions

  • Act as gatekeeper for European Union outside counsel engagements: scope the work, estimate and manage cost, and sign off before matters go externally

  • Mentor and develop more junior lawyers in the team, set quality standards for plain-English, risk-based advice, and act as a senior sounding board for colleagues across the Regulatory Legal team

  • Use AI-assisted tools (for example Enterprise GPTs) to speed up regulatory analysis, first drafts and matter tracking, and to build self-service tools that let stakeholders answer commoditised legal and regulatory questions themselves

  • Advise on anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing requirements affecting products, including the Transfer of Funds Regulation ("Travel Rule") and the new European Union anti-money laundering package, and on market abuse, conduct, outsourcing and operational resilience obligations, including the Digital Operational Resilience Act ("DORA")

  • Lead or oversee licensing, authorisation and variation workstreams in the European Union, including scoping requirements, mapping pathways, supervising outside counsel, preparing application materials and managing regulator interactions

 
 

What you bring

  • Qualified lawyer admitted in Ireland, England and Wales, or another European Union Member State

  • 15 or more years' post-qualification experience ("PQE") in financial services regulatory law, gained at a regulated financial services institution (for example a bank, payment institution, broker-dealer, exchange, central counterparty or crypto services provider) or at a leading law firm supporting such clients, ideally with in-house or direct product counselling experience

  • Deep, current knowledge of several of the following, with real depth in at least two: MiFID II and MiFIR (investment services, market structure, derivatives and conduct), MiCA (crypto-asset services, custody, trading platforms and stablecoins), European Union payment services and electronic money regulation, and European Union banking regulation

  • Demonstrated ability to analyse novel products against overlapping regimes and give a clear view on classification and perimeter, including in areas where the rules are unsettled or supervisors have not yet spoken

  • Direct experience managing senior regulator relationships, including notifications, information requests, supervisory correspondence and examinations

  • Working knowledge of anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing, outsourcing and operational resilience obligations, including DORA

  • Proven ability to instruct, supervise and manage the cost of outside counsel across multiple jurisdictions

  • Outstanding analytical, drafting and organisational skills, with crisp, plain-English writing

  • Ability to distill complex legal and regulatory issues into clear, actionable guidance for non-lawyer stakeholders and for senior leadership

  • A pragmatic, commercially accountable approach to legal and regulatory risk that gives stakeholders a useful range of options and a clear recommendation

  • Experience mentoring or managing lawyers, and the judgement to know when to escalate

  • Comfort operating with a high degree of autonomy in a fast-moving, remote environment

  • Familiarity with using AI tools such as Enterprise GPTs to increase the efficiency of legal services

 
 

Nice to haves

  • Experience advising on tokenised securities and the European Union Distributed Ledger Technology Pilot Regime

  • Experience with EMIR, including the clearing obligation, margin for non-centrally cleared derivatives and transaction reporting

  • Experience with prime brokerage, securities financing, margin lending or institutional custody

  • Experience advising on the United Kingdom cryptoasset regime or other non-European Union frameworks that intersect with European Union operations

  • Experience supporting regulatory aspects of corporate transactions, such as change-of-control notifications and entity migrations

  • Experience with European Union data protection and consumer protection rules as they apply to financial products

  • Fluency in a second European language

  • An authentic interest in crypto and digital assets, and familiarity with Payward's and competitors' products

  • Run it and write it up. Execute the evaluation, do the statistics, and write it up once in a form that serves the pod, the regulatory file and an academic submission.
